authoring_guidance: Write the final answer for a traveler in natural travel-advisor language. Give the useful result first, then concise Option A/B/C sections with exact local departure and arrival dates. A compact table is welcome when it genuinely improves comparison. Each option should read like an itinerary summary, not a field-by-field data export. Do not show raw IDs, UTC, internal status words, machine codes, query types, or validation language. Use a short visible stable identifier for every option. Every selected journey must visibly bind these exact keys somewhere in its own journey parts or through valid shared_disclosures: status, styles, route, departure, arrival, elapsed, award_program, award_route, award_departure, award_arrival, award_carrier, award_cabin, award_leg_cabins, points, fees, award_price_scope, price_completeness, booking_obligation, requirements, award_observed_at. If a journey has a cash component, also bind transfer, cash, cash_cabin, cash_leg_cabins, cash_route, cash_departure, cash_arrival, cash_price_scope, cash_observed_at. Bind award_mixed_cabin_pct or cash_mixed_cabin_pct when a reported value requires them. For selected direct cash comparison use a visible identifier such as Cash price comparison and bind disposition, route, departure, arrival, observed_at, provider_updated_at, cash, price_scope, carrier, cabin, leg_cabins. For an incomplete lead use a visible identifier and bind disposition, route, departure, arrival, observed_at, provider_updated_at. In the shared introduction bind provider_status and coverage; also bind complete_journey_count when there are zero complete journeys, and benchmark_status when no benchmark is selected. Treat each slot as the full text it supplies. Departure and arrival already include both date and local time: write 'Leave {{fact:departure}}' without another date or 'at'. Currency and points slots already include units. Quote-scope slots may be whole sentences: place them as standalone text (for example, '{{fact:award_price_scope}}') and never inside 'scope is ...'. Place status/styles in one short natural sentence near the option's lead, and the award program in its booking sentence. Keep mandatory cabin and price caveats once per applicable option; do not restate the same uncertainty in a second paragraph. Shared facts may be shown once only when their exact slot values match for all bound options, and the shared part visibly names each Option A/B/C target. Do not claim no unresolved requirements from an admitted status; price limitations and unknowns still matter. Do not infer all-in or party-total cost, current seats, bookability, protection, or leg cabins. If you declare a material claim, copy its claim.text literally into visible prose in the same part and use only a true applicable predicate; omit gratuitous claims. Make headings and option descriptions useful to a traveler and keep punctuation natural. Parts concatenate without separators, so include blank lines. On correction fix every missing key and claim failure before editing style. Choose genuinely useful, distinct alternatives from the supplied complete set: explain a supported tradeoff such as an earlier arrival, premium cabin, or lower observed fees against longer travel, or select fewer options when a variant is redundant. Do not make fastest, cheapest, or superior-value claims about the full pool without the exact supported comparison predicate. Keep any difference tied to the displayed route, date, duration, cabin, or observed amount. The conditional and incomplete cases still require honest traveler-facing answers; do not hide them or turn incomplete leads into recommendations.
